resolutions.target_artifact: specs/tail-recall/spec.md, requirement "A recall block does not cost the turn its cached prefix", scenario "In-turn requests" (THEN)
resolutions.rationale:
CHURN: this scenario is my own s3-r3 remedy (critic-r3-1, item 3), and it sits in the requirement that was patched last round.

The finding is correct. On a later request of the turn, the write depends on what the turn's first request did with the block.
- **First request kept pi's marker on the block** (it recalled after a turn that recalled nothing): the block was cached, and the second request writes only the new step.
- **First request removed pi's marker** (a handoff that also recalled): the block went out as input. The second request's breakpoint is pi's marker on the new `tool_result`, which sits after the block, so it writes the block as well as the step.

The context-figures table already prices this second case at the write rate ("cached, and new to the last priced request or left uncached by it: the write rate"). As written, the two spec files disagree about the same request.
resolutions.required_change:
Replace the THEN of "In-turn requests" with:

> "pi's marker stays on the last `tool_result`, so the request writes the new step, plus recall's block when the turn's first request billed it as input. Measured: 83 written after a first request that kept the block cached (N9, turn 2, request 2), and 2,682 and 2,675 written after a handoff that also recalled (N3, turn 2, request 2; N9, turn 3, request 2). The block is priced by context-figures' \"The block's charge, by placement and request\"."

Not run as new work: wording only, and the figures were read from the logs above.

resolutions.target_artifact: design.md §8.1 adapter tests; §8.3 Preconditions and a new set of assertions on turn 2, request 1
resolutions.rationale:
The finding is correct. No adapter test and no live assertion covers the most common recalling request: the one that wants only the before point.

- **No adapter test catches the backwards implementation.** An implementation that removes pi's marker whenever any point is placed passes every test in §8.1. The handoff tests expect removal anyway; the in-place test checks only the before point; the coincident-carry test places nothing.
- **The live script never asserts on this case.** Turn 2, request 1 is exactly it: turn 1 carries no block because the archive fills only at settlement, so record (b) is null.
- **The critic's billing bound is the wrong side.** `write ≥ ⌈chars(block)/8⌉` does not discriminate in this script. Turn 2's own text is an 800-entry table of 10,199 characters, about 2,900 tokens. It is written regardless of where pi's marker sits, and that alone exceeds `⌈chars(block)/8⌉` = 1,737 for the recalled `seq 1 3000` output (13,892 characters), so a broken run would still pass.
- **The input bound does discriminate.** A cached block leaves `input` near zero (3 in N9). An uncached block puts its own tokens into `input` (2,597 for a block whose `⌈chars/8⌉` is 1,040). This mirrors the existing `input_H` assertion.
resolutions.evidence:
- `s-key-h45-r23.log` (N9), turn 2, request 1: input 3 against the probe block's `⌈8,315 / 8⌉` = 1,040, so the bound passes.
- The same log's turn 3, request 1, where the block was uncached: input 2,597 ≥ 1,040, so a backwards implementation would fail the bound.
- Character counts computed this pass: probe2's block 8,315; `seq 1 3000` 13,892; an 800-entry table 10,199.
- design.md §8.1 and §8.3, read.

resolutions.target_artifact: design.md D8 (`applied.block` derivation) and §5.3 (5); §8.1 adapter tests
resolutions.rationale:
The finding is correct. D8 says `applied.block` is "null only when the request carries no block". §11 says it is null when pi's marking drifts. The Joel-route lone-surrogate case reaches a third state: cell (a) is set, but no payload block matches it.

The adapter knows recall's block only by finding the carrier, so with no match it cannot place "recall's block or any block after it" at all. The rule has to be written on what the adapter can see.

Null is also the correct outcome for that case. With no carrier, at most the carry is wanted, 1 + 1 fits budget 2, and pi's marker stays on the newest message's last block. The block is therefore cached and written, and null prices the cached rows.
resolutions.evidence:
- design.md D8 and §5.3 (5): "null only when the request carries no block".
- design.md §11, "pi's marking could drift": "`applied.block` is null".
- design.md §6.1, lone-surrogate row: on Joel's route the payload carries U+FFFD, so there is no match (`dr-s3-r2.log`).

In D8 and §5.3 (5), replace "null only when the request carries no block" with "null when no carrier is found, which includes a request carrying no block".

Add one adapter test to §8.1: cell (a) set and no payload block equal to it. `applied.block` is null, and no before point is placed.

resolutions.target_artifact: design.md §7.3 and §11; specs/context-figures/spec.md scenario "The under-reporting is recorded where the figure is read"; the README under-reporting record (docs pass)
resolutions.rationale:
CHURN: part (b) adds a bullet to §11, which was patched last round. Part (a) lands on §7.3 and the context-figures scenario, which were not.

Both gaps are real, and neither needs mechanism.

**(a) The budget-1 tail is cost the figure never sees.** §11 already accepts the cost. At budget 1, every in-turn request moves pi's marker off the tail, so each step re-sends the tool-result tail as input instead of reading it. The figure has no term for that: `blockChanged` is false in-turn, so the rewrite term is 0, and D8 charges only the block. Under Q3(a) and the ruling "under-reporting home", every known under-report is recorded in the README.

**(b) A provider that never calls `onPayload` leaves the previous `applied` in place.** taiknr's hook then never fires, and the next valid `message_end` prices with the earlier placement.
- Every built-in pi-ai streaming API calls `onPayload`. pi's custom-provider contract requires it.
- So the case needs an extension-registered provider that breaks that contract.
- Guarding it would need a second writer to `applied`, which the §5.1 ordering exists to avoid. Record it.
resolutions.evidence:
- `rg -c onPayload` over pi-ai's `dist/api/*.js` finds one call in each streaming API: anthropic-messages, azure-openai-responses, bedrock-converse-stream, google-generative-ai, google-vertex, mistral-conversations, openai-codex-responses, openai-completions, openai-responses, pi-messages and openrouter-images.
- pi `docs/custom-provider.md:195`: "Call `options.onPayload` before sending the provider request and use any replacement payload it returns … Omitting them makes the provider behave differently from Pi's built-in providers."
- design.md §11, "Budget 1 bills the in-turn tail as input", already quantifies (a).
resolutions.required_change:
**(a) Record the budget-1 tail.**
- **§7.3:** add "requests where another extension's marker leaves budget 1: each in-turn step re-sends the turn's tool-result tail as input, and the figure charges only the block (§11)".
- **context-figures "The under-reporting is recorded where the figure is read", THEN:** extend the list with "and on in-turn requests where another extension's marker leaves budget 1".
- **Docs pass:** the README under-reporting record names the same case.

**(b) §11, one bullet:**

> "**A provider that never calls `onPayload` prices with stale state.** Concrete case: a covered handoff that also recalls leaves `applied = { block: \"uncached\", carrierRead: R }`, then `/model` switches to an extension-registered provider whose `streamSimple` ignores `options.onPayload`. That request's block is priced at the input rate, and its baseline stores `blockUncached: true`, so the next request is charged the write rate for a read. pi requires custom streams to call it (`docs/custom-provider.md:195`), and every built-in API does. Recorded, not guarded: a guard would be a second writer to `applied`."

Not run: recording only.

resolutions.target_artifact: design.md §5.3 (4) "A marker, and pi's message marker", §6.1 (new row) and §11; specs/tail-recall/spec.md scenarios "A payload pi marked nowhere" and "Another extension's marker survives"
resolutions.rationale:
CHURN: "A payload pi marked nowhere" sits under the requirement "Only routes the predicate covers change", which was patched last round, and the fix adds a bullet to §11, also patched last round.

The finding is correct, and I reproduced it.
- **The gap.** Recognition by count, which I ruled in dr-s2 cc2-1, cannot tell a lone foreign message marker from pi's when pi marked nothing.
- **The case.** With `cacheRetention` none and one message marker placed by an extension loaded before taiknr, the measured logic takes that marker as pi's. It copies the marker as its template. When foreign top-level, system or tools markers bring the budget below the wanted points plus one, it removes that marker as "pi's last-message marker".
- **My ruling 1 is narrowed.** Its "if pi placed no message marker, nothing is edited" now holds only when the payload carries no message-level marker at all.

**Why this is recorded, not guarded.**
- Provenance cannot be read from the payload.
- Any heuristic (a system marker present alongside, matching marker shapes) can be defeated by a foreign extension and is unmeasured on Joel's route.
- Count-based recognition measured clean on 152 of 152 requests.
- The trigger needs `cacheRetention` none, which is an explicit opt-out, plus a foreign extension that places exactly one message marker and loads before taiknr. The removal additionally needs foreign non-message markers.
- A copied point adds no cost and is TTL-safe, because it is a copy.

The mechanism stays as ruled. The spec's guarantees are narrowed to what it can keep.
resolutions.evidence:
`.pi/marbleization/cache-point-before-recall/michael/dr-s3-r4-lone.mjs`, output in `dr-s3-r4-lone.log`. It is probe2's measured count-based logic, with pi marking nothing and one foreign 1h marker on an older message.
- In: [m[0][0] foreign]. Out: [m[0][0] foreign, m[2][0] a copy of the foreign marker], so the payload was edited although pi marked nothing.
- With foreign top-level, system and tools markers (budget 1). In: [top, system[0], tools[0], m[0][0] foreign]. Out: [top, system[0], tools[0], m[2][0] copy], so the foreign marker on m[0][0] was removed.

Ruling text: michael-council-rulings.json row 1.
resolutions.required_change:
**§5.3 (4), "A marker, and pi's message marker".** Append:

> "A lone message-level marker placed by another extension on a payload pi marked nowhere is indistinguishable from pi's and is treated as pi's: copied, and on a spent budget removed (§11)."

**§6.1, new row.** "A lone message-level marker that is not pi's, where pi marked nowhere": treated as pi's, so the edit runs and copies it, and the marker is removed when the wanted points plus one do not fit (§11).

**§11, one bullet:**

> "**A lone foreign message marker is taken for pi's.** Concrete case: `cacheRetention` none, so pi marks nothing; an extension loaded before taiknr places one message-level marker, with foreign top-level, system and tools markers leaving budget 1. taiknr copies that marker as its before point and removes the original as pi's last-message marker, so the other extension loses its entry (`dr-s3-r4-lone.log`). Provenance is not observable from the payload, and the trigger needs an explicit caching opt-out plus that extension, so it is recorded and not guarded."

**Spec "A payload pi marked nowhere".**
- WHEN: "pi places no message-level cache marker and no other extension placed one either".
- Append to THEN: "A lone marker another extension placed where pi marked nothing cannot be told from pi's and is treated as pi's (design §11)."

**Spec "Another extension's marker survives".** WHEN: "another extension placed a message-level marker beside pi's".

Run status: the case ran against the measured logic (`dr-s3-r4-lone.log`).

settled_findings: An in-turn request writes the new step, plus recall's block when the turn's first request billed it as input. Measured: 83 after a cached first request (N9, turn 2, request 2), and 2,682 and 2,675 after a handoff that also recalled (N3; N9, turn 3, request 2).

The live check for a before-point-only request bounds `input`, not `write`. The live script's turn-2 table (10,199 chars) is written wherever pi's marker sits, so a write bound cannot discriminate. `input_R1 < ⌈chars(block)/8⌉` passes at 3 against 1,040 on N9 and fails on an uncached block (2,597).
`applied.block` is null when no carrier is found, which includes a request carrying no block, and null prices the cached rows.

Count-based recognition of pi's message marker stands (152/152). A lone foreign message marker on a payload pi marked nowhere is treated as pi's. This is recorded, not guarded (`dr-s3-r4-lone.log`), and it narrows council ruling 1.

A provider that never calls `options.onPayload` leaves the previous `applied` in place. This is recorded, not guarded, because a guard would need a second writer to `applied`. pi requires custom streams to call it (`docs/custom-provider.md:195`), and every built-in API does.
